Definition: to blow; by implication, to disperse
BiblicalUsage: Abram drives the birds of prey away from the sacrifice, scattering them before they can touch it, and the breath of the LORD blows on the grass so that it withers and the flower fades.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God's breath is stronger than anything it falls on: it scatters what threatens His offering, and it withers what stands proud in its own strength.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
